purpose: Ensure every public exact point represents the event's actual supported site, never a nearby or representative coordinate.

required: semantic site validation against the event location claim or source geometry
authoritative or approved exact-address geocoder result
two independently resolved authoritative endpoints or explicit certified reference
midpoint derived only from certified endpoints
prohibited: Planning Labs GeoSearch midpoint as certification authority
legacy coordinate reuse without canonical re-resolution

required: authoritative facility, park, or venue identifier
boundary containment when facility geometry exists

non_point_events.route_event: Use exact route/line geometry or an explicitly supported route anchor when the source defines one; never fabricate a midpoint point.
non_point_events.area_event: Use exact area/polygon geometry when supported; otherwise retain as non-point/list presentation.
non_point_events.citywide_event: Retain and display without a fabricated exact point unless the source identifies a specific site.

release_accounting.accepted_occurrence_equation: accepted = exact_point + exact_route_or_area + retained_location_pending + explicit_non_point_disposition + dedupe_with_lineage

per_event_exactness_goal.target: Resolve every accepted event to the most precise location the source evidence can truthfully support.
per_event_exactness_goal.important_constraint: Do not force a point for events whose real-world footprint is a route, area, multi-site activity, or unspecified location. Exactness means faithful geometry, not necessarily Point geometry.

regression_examples: East 74 Street between Avenue U and Avenue T must remain Brooklyn and must not regress to a nearby/wrong-block point.
A park-level centroid must not stand in for a named event site inside a large park.
An official source coordinate must remain non-public as an exact pin until event-site agreement is validated.
